To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maximum entropy reinforcement learning maximizes a robust reinforcement learning objective, and thus has robustness guarantees.

1) the MaxEnt RL objective is a lower bound on the robust RL objective, 2) the robust RL objective can be written as the sum of the standard RL objective and a term involving the entropy of the learned policy, and 3) the robust set of MaxEnt RL is non-empty, and can contain the entire state space for certain disturbances to the dynamics and the rewards.

(a) MaxEnt RL is robust to certain classes of disturbances in the dynamics or reward functions; (b) MaxEnt RL can be used to solve certain robust RL problems without requiring additional moving parts or hyperparameters; and (c) the MaxEnt RL objective is the first objective that we are aware of for which we have a rigorous characterization of a robust set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical understanding of the robustness properties of MaxEnt RL, which we hope will lead to a deeper understanding of the robust RL problem and to improved robust RL algorithms.
understanding the robustness of MaxEnt RL.
the question: can a single RL method, without any additional moving parts, be used to robustify a wide class of RL algorithms?

our results suggest that the MaxEnt RL objective can be used to solve some robust RL problems, without the need to add additional components to the algorithm.
MaxEnt RL (provably) solves some robust RL problems.
we provide the first provable robust RL algorithm that is simple, practical, and effective in practice, and we believe that this is an exciting result that will have a large impact.

we provide a theoretical justification that MaxEnt RL can be viewed as robust RL.

a simple, widely used RL method is already robust to certain disturbances.
